title: Tako the Piano-Playing Octopus Hangs Up His Tentacles
summary:
Have you ever seen an octopus play the piano? Probably not! But a clever octopus named Tako did just that. And now, after becoming a viral star, Tako has retired.

Tako's owner is a Swedish YouTuber named Mattias Krantz. He always dreamed of teaching an animal to play music. Octopuses are super smart—about as smart as a three-year-old kid—and each of their eight arms has its own mini brain. So Krantz thought, why not?

But teaching an octopus piano wasn't easy. Octopuses can't hear sounds in the air, so Krantz added a speaker that vibrated the water so Tako could feel the music. Also, octopuses like to pull things, not push them. So Krantz built a special keyboard with keys you pull. And to reward Tako, he made a "crab elevator" that lowered a live crab into the tank when Tako played the right notes. Yum!

After six months of practice, Tako learned to play sequences of notes. Krantz made a video showing Tako playing along with his guitar. It went viral! But octopuses don't live very long. Tako is now old and tired. Instead of making more videos, Krantz turned off the cameras so Tako can rest in his favorite cave. What a nice way to say goodbye to a musical friend.
why_it_matters: This shows that with patience and kind training, animals can learn surprising things, and it is important to let older animals rest and be comfortable.

background_read: Octopuses are real ocean animals with eight arms, and scientists study them because they are very good at solving puzzles.
Mattias Krantz (the Swedish YouTuber who trained Tako) often builds unusual machines and films his experiments.
Many animal videos become viral when millions of people watch and share them in a short time.
Article_Structure: WHO: Tako the octopus and his owner, Swedish YouTuber Mattias Krantz.
WHAT: Tako learned to play piano and later retired from making videos.
WHERE: In a special tank with a pull-keyboard and a crab elevator.
WHY: Tako is old and tired, and octopuses do not live very long, so Krantz turned off the cameras so Tako can rest.

perspectives.description: The videos showed how smart octopuses can be and helped people understand animals in a fun way.
Some people might worry about keeping a clever octopus in a tank or using live crabs as practice rewards.
Krantz decided to stop filming so Tako could rest, which shows respect for the octopus's age and health.
